title: Perfect-matching contraction transition quotient
statement: Let G be cubic with a perfect matching M. Contract every edge of M. Each quotient vertex inherits a 2+2 partition of its four incident half-edges according to the two endpoints of the matching edge.

title: Switching-cycle lift
statement: Every simple switching r-cycle in the quotient of TR01 lifts to an M-alternating simple cycle of length 2r in G.

title: Alternating-cycle contraction correspondence
statement: M-alternating cycles in G correspond bijectively to simple switching cycles in the quotient, with lengths divided by 2 under contraction.

title: Switching-circuit existence
statement: After choosing one cross-pairing at every quotient vertex, the quotient edges decompose into closed switching circuits.

title: Alternating-cycle flip
statement: If C is an M-alternating cycle of length 2r, then M triangle E(C) is a perfect matching M_C with |M\M_C|=|M_C\M|=r.

title: Perfect-matching symmetric-difference decomposition
statement: For any two perfect matchings M,M', the symmetric difference M triangle M' is a disjoint union of even cycles alternating between the two matchings.

title: Exchange-distance sum formula
statement: If the components of M triangle M' have lengths 2r_1,...,2r_t, then |M\M'|=r_1+...+r_t.

title: Odd-lock exchange congruence
statement: Let g(M) be the gcd of the half-lengths of all M-alternating cycles. Then g(M) divides |M\M'| for every perfect matching M'.

title: Odd-lock exact equivalence
statement: For fixed M and integer g>=1, every M-alternating cycle has half-length divisible by g if and only if every perfect matching M' satisfies |M\M'| divisible by g; equivalently |M intersect M'| congruent to |M| modulo g.

title: Modular constant-weight formulation
statement: For an odd prime p, p divides g(M) exactly when the indicator weight 1_M has the same total modulo p on every perfect matching.

title: Odd-lock order divisibility
statement: The odd part of g(M) divides |M|=|V(G)|/2.

title: Power-of-two matching-size exclusion
statement: If |M| is a power of two, then g(M) has no odd divisor.

title: Node-potential alternating law
statement: Assume over an odd prime field that 1_M(uv)=alpha(u)+alpha(v) for every edge. Then alpha alternates sign around every component of the 2-factor G-M.

title: Odd 2-factor component zero law
statement: Under TR13, every vertex on an odd cycle component of G-M has alpha=0; consequently an M-edge cannot join two odd components.

title: Complementary-channel lemma
statement: At every vertex of a switching cycle C, the two edges not used by C form the complementary permissible switching transition.

title: Opposite-port compatibility
statement: Orient C and label its unused ports + and - according to which incident cycle edge they can switch onto. An external switching route combines with an arc of C exactly when its endpoint signs are opposite.

title: Odd-cycle compatible-return theorem
statement: For an odd switching cycle C, every complete deterministic pairing of the exterior transitions contains an opposite-sign boundary route and hence a compatible return trail.

title: Return-trail shortestness bound
statement: Let C be a shortest switching cycle of length r. If a compatible return route P plus its compatible arc A decomposes into t simple switching cycles, then |P|+|A|>=tr.

title: Subdouble-return simplicity
statement: Under BR04, if |P|+|A|<2r, then P union A is a single simple switching cycle.

title: Route-mass conservation
statement: Switching the local exterior pairing at one vertex preserves the sum of the lengths of the two affected boundary routes.

title: Endpoint-displacement conservation
statement: A local exterior pairing switch preserves the multiset of four boundary endpoints; with a fixed orientation convention, the signed sum of the two affected boundary displacements is conserved modulo |C|.

title: Boundary sign-exchange identity
statement: At the pairing level, re-pairing one (+,+) route and one (-,-) route crosswise creates two opposite-sign routes.

title: Residue-class leakage dichotomy
statement: Let |C|=2^s u with u odd, and partition boundary positions by residue modulo 2^s. For each residue class, every complete boundary pairing either contains an opposite-sign pair internal to that class, or has at least one positive and at least one negative port paired outside the class.

title: Residue leakage lower bound
statement: If no residue class in BR09 contains an internal opposite-sign pair, then at least 2^s boundary routes connect different residue classes.

title: Power-safe cubic bridge elimination
statement: Every minimum-order cubic counterexample is bridgeless, or every bridge side admits a smaller cubic completion whose dyadic cycles lift to the original graph.

title: Universal-root dyadic return theorem
statement: If delta(G)>=3 and G-v is 2-degenerate for every v, then some v has neighbors x,y joined in G-v by a path of length 2^k-2.

title: Dyadic Laman-circuit theorem
statement: Every graph with m=2n-2, delta>=3, and e(S)<=2|S|-3 for every proper S contains a power-of-two cycle.

title: Power-safe Henneberg reduction
statement: Every dense-branch sparse circuit contains a degree-3 reduction whose smaller dyadic cycle lifts to a dyadic cycle in the original graph.

title: Slack discharge theorem
statement: Every slack-branch minimum candidate with |A|-D>=6 contains a finite reducible cubic configuration or a power-of-two cycle.

title: Two-forest dyadic fundamental-cycle theorem
statement: For every minimum counterexample two-forest decomposition F0 union F1, some cross-forest edge has fundamental-cycle length a power of two in one direction, or after swapping the forests.

title: Concentrated selected-radius expansion
statement: The concentrated vertex from DS16 cannot sustain pairwise separated branches through every connector radius 2^k-2 in a finite minimum-degree-3 graph.

title: Power-safe defect absorption
statement: Every noncubic minimum candidate admits a quotient or state expansion eliminating branching cubic defects while multiplying all lifted cycle lengths by a fixed power of two.

title: Matching-choice odd-lock destruction
statement: Every bridgeless cubic graph has a perfect matching M for which g(M) has no odd prime divisor.

title: Three-matching coprimality theorem
statement: Every bridgeless cubic graph has perfect matchings M,M1,M2 such that the odd part of gcd(|M\M1|,|M\M2|) is 1.

title: Modular matching-lattice theorem
statement: Classify F_p-valued edge weights on matching-covered cubic graphs that have constant total on every perfect matching, with explicit tight-cut and brick/brace alternatives.

title: Tight-cut exchange synthesis
statement: Across a tight-cut decomposition, compatible local perfect-matching exchanges synthesize global exchange distances d1,d2,d1+d2, forcing any odd lock to descend to an active factor.

title: Brick/brace indicator exclusion
statement: In a minimal matching block, the indicator of a perfect matching cannot be a nontrivial constant modular perfect-matching weight in odd characteristic.

title: Primitive dyadic member realization
statement: If the gcd of M-alternating half-lengths is a power of two, then for some suitable perfect matching representation an actual alternating half-length is a power of two.

title: Odd shortest-cycle dyadic steering
statement: For an odd shortest switching cycle C of length r, some exterior transition pairing has an opposite-sign route P whose compatible arc A satisfies |P|+|A|=2^ceil(log2 r).

title: Residue-preserving descent
statement: For a shortest switching cycle of length 2^s u with u odd and greater than 1, some exterior pairing yields a shorter switching cycle whose length remains divisible by 2^s.

title: Length-displacement exchange theorem
statement: In the exterior pairing-exchange graph around a shortest switching cycle, either some route label (length, displacement) closes to a dyadic cycle, a local switch creates a shorter switching cycle, or the routing lies in an explicitly classifiable rigid family.

title: Exchange-rigid periodicity classification
statement: Every exterior routing rigid under all local pairing switches is a periodic cover of the boundary cycle and admits either a smaller quotient or an arithmetic progression of switching-cycle lengths.

title: Flat plateau impossibility
statement: A shortest switching cycle cannot be surrounded by a completely flat positive-error plateau in the exterior pairing-exchange graph unless TG18 periodicity holds.

title: Finite transition hostile-system classification
statement: Every minimal 4-regular 2+2 transition system hostile to TG15-TG17 belongs to a finite catalog of exchange-rigid templates.

title: Bounded-surplus defect-core classification
statement: For each fixed t, all noncubic minimum candidates with |A|=2|B|+t reduce to finitely many defect-core topologies of size at most 6t attached to an ordinary quotient on B.

title: Defect-core cycle-lifting dichotomy
statement: Every bounded defect core either admits a power-safe quotient to a smaller minimum-degree-3 graph or forces a power-of-two cycle locally.

title: Cubic-edge C4/C8 extension classification
statement: For adjacent cubic vertices u,v, every legal radius-3 extension avoiding C4 and C8 belongs to a finite list, each reducible or forcing a longer dyadic connector.

title: Induced-path contact-to-dyadic compiler
statement: Every sufficiently long induced path in a minimum counterexample has an outside contact pattern producing a dyadic cycle or a reducible configuration.

title: Full flagship closure program
statement: Every finite simple graph of minimum degree at least 3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.

title: Attachment-hypergraph non-universality
statement: The high-degree attachment hypergraph cannot be a universal primary representation of a minimum counterexample.

title: Width-two three-terminal forcing is false
statement: Two-degeneracy plus three degree-2 terminals does not force a connector of length 2^k-2.

title: Two-forest word doubling is false
statement: Being the union of two forests does not by itself force a dyadic cycle or binary doubling law.

title: Sparse rigidity alone is insufficient
statement: The density inequalities m<=2n-2 and e(S)<=2|S|-3 alone do not determine dyadic cycle lengths.

title: Edge-spectrum primacy sterility
statement: The edge return-spectrum reformulation is not a compression without a theorem selecting an edge with sufficiently rich return paths.

title: Integer splicing cannot break an odd lock
statement: If every available switching-circuit length is divisible by an odd integer p, then any length obtained solely by integer sums and differences remains divisible by p; such arithmetic splicing cannot produce a power of two.

title: Power-of-two gcd does not imply a dyadic member
statement: A set of positive integers may have gcd a power of two while containing no power of two.

title: Transition-cocycle equivalence withdrawn
statement: The proposed equivalence between odd lock and a nontrivial transition cocycle is not established and must not be used as a Court edge.

title: Two-arc ear compatibility is impossible
statement: For an external switching ear attached to a switching cycle in a 2+2 transition system, at most one of the two boundary arcs is compatible with the ear.

title: Local minimum does not imply path independence
statement: A local minimum in the exterior pairing-exchange graph does not imply commuting squares, zero discrete curvature, or path-independent objective changes.

title: Canonical-ear continuity withdrawn
statement: Shortest external returns from neighboring boundary ports need not vary continuously in endpoint or total cycle length.
